title: VPC post-launch compact smoke + incremental load walkthrough
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Purpose: Define and implement a compact, repeatable post-deploy verification that runs automatically after Terraform apply for Private (VPC) deployments. This ticket covers a focused smoke + incremental-load walkthrough that validates: 1) API endpoint readiness (TLS + auth + routing), 2) model process initialization and KV-cache warmup, 3) short burst and ramped concurrency model-load checks across representative sequence lengths, and 4) observable SLO gates (p50/p95 latency, qps, token/sec, error budget delta).

Scope: 
- A minimal test plan and scripts (bash/python) that CI/CD can run as a postapply hook.
- Integration with probe-runner v2 (local runner container) to execute endpoint and model checks.
- Compact load profiles: smoke (1 req/s for 60s), incremental ramp (1 -> 40 concurrent over 10 mins), and KV-cache warmup scenarios (prefix cache hits validation).
- Clear success criteria (see below) and logging/telemetry links.

Success criteria (all must pass unless explicitly waived):
- API handshake completes and returns 200 within 2s for health endpoint and 95% within 500ms for internal readiness probe.
- Model instantiation completes (first-token latency) under 6s for target model family (quantized variants allowed), and remains stable under smoke load.
- KV cache hit-rate increases to >60% after warmup sequence and token/sec improves correspondingly.
- No increase in 5xx rate above baseline + 0.5% during test window.
- Runbook artifacts created and linked to console dashboards for the rollout wave.

Non-goals: full-scale soak or long-duration performance testing; those remain in dedicated load suites. This is intended as an inexpensive gate for automated post-deploy checks.
notes: This ticket is intentionally compact to fit inside the postapply window for most Dedicated/Private customers. We trade off deep statistical coverage for speed and determinism (short fixed windows, deterministic inputs). For teams wanting larger tests we will chain into existing load jobs (dependents listed).
